set: WCXB test split, local copy data/wcxb/test
scorer: poc.wcxb.word_f1 and snippet_rate (tokenizer \w+ lower-cased; same as data/wcxb/evaluate.py)
interval_method: paired difference per page; sites (registrable domain, poc.psl) resampled with replacement; 5,000 draws; numpy default_rng(0); 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles
note: Default API and CLI output are the same: `chromerag extract page.html --url URL` writes ExtractResult.markdown, and the CLI config equals PipelineConfig.from_priority(mode) (checked). ChromeRAG front matter (enable_schema=True, default) is a YAML block between --- lines built by schema_fusion.fuse_front_matter: url (the url argument), title (<title>, else og:title; replaced by a JSON-LD/microdata headline or name), description (meta description, replaced by Schema.org description), type (Schema.org @type of the main node), lastUpdated (dateModified, datePublished or lastUpdated), author (Schema.org author name) and breadcrumb (JSON-LD BreadcrumbList names joined by ' > '). Trafilatura 2.2.0 with with_metadata=True and output_format='markdown' prepends its own YAML block; keys seen on these pages (counts in front_matter.trafilatura_meta): url, hostname, sitename, title, date, description, author, tags, categories, license, each only when found. Without metadata Trafilatura emits no block. ChromeRAG emits its block even when the body is empty, so raw output is never empty. 'raw' scores the text as emitted; 'stripped' removes one leading YAML block with the regex of poc.wcxb.strip_front_matter (the method of the final run). The WCXB reference holds body text only, so metadata words count against precision. Trafilatura settings otherwise as poc/baselines.py (tables on, comments and links off, url given).
text_correction: 2026-11-20: note text on the Trafilatura key list corrected after reading the key counts; scores unchanged.
